question: After generic sequence context and observable boundary structure are accounted for, does recurring glyph identity contribute a transferable residual transition law, and can those laws be compressed into a finite inventory of action-equivalent operator classes that predicts unseen inscriptions?
codeClaim: A positive result supports the operational claim that part of the corpus behaves as a finite code: recurring glyph identities contribute stable state-transition rules that can be learned on one set of inscriptions, compressed into a finite machine, and run forward on unseen inscriptions.

source.inscriptionKeyUse: lane assignment and anonymous custody id only

lanes.assignment: sha256(inscription map key) first 64-bit integer modulo 10
lanes.rule: Only train may define vocabulary, eligible glyph operators, smoothing tables, functional fingerprints, operator classes, class count, or thresholds. Holdout and control are evaluation-only.

sequence.boundaryAware: Within each inscription, preserve order inside each raw words token; insert <WORD> between adjacent non-newline words and <LINE> at each raw newline.
sequence.lineOnly: Preserve raw glyph order and <LINE> boundaries but remove word boundaries.
sequence.inscriptionBoundary: <DOC> is placed before the first and after the last sequence item.
sequence.operator: One recurring raw Unicode glyph codepoint at the current position. Boundary tokens are states and never operators.
sequence.incomingState: The immediately preceding stream item after train-vocabulary mapping.
sequence.outgoingState: The immediately following stream item after train-vocabulary mapping.

model.operatorKernel: K_g(s_out | s_in), hierarchically smoothed to P0
model.operatorGain: mean log2 P_K - mean log2 P0 on evaluation occurrences
model.fingerprint: For each eligible glyph, concatenate train input-state-weighted residual vectors K_g(.|s_in)-P0(.|s_in) over supported incoming states.

functionalClasses.selection: Train-only deterministic agglomerative average-link clustering of operator fingerprints. Choose class count by minimum five-fold inscription-hash cross-validated class-model log loss with a BIC-style complexity penalty of 0.5 * parameters * ln(events) / events.
functionalClasses.classKernel: K_C(s_out | s_in) learned from train occurrences pooled across frozen class members and smoothed to P0.
functionalClasses.actionEquivalenceTest: On holdout/control, the finite class model must beat context-only and retain a declared fraction of the glyph-specific operator gain.

adjudication.finiteOperationalCodeTransfers: Both holdout and control clear coverage/source support; glyph-specific kernels beat context-only by the operator gain gate; the frozen finite class model beats context-only and retains the required fraction of glyph-specific gain.
adjudication.operatorCodeWithoutFiniteQuotient: Glyph-specific kernels transfer but the frozen finite class inventory does not retain enough of their gain.
adjudication.sequenceIdentityWithoutTransfer: Train discovers operator residuals but they do not improve untouched inscriptions.
adjudication.noResidualGlyphCodeUnderV10: Glyph identity does not materially improve prediction beyond generic preceding-state and boundary context on holdout.
adjudication.boundaryDependence: If boundaryAware passes but lineOnly fails, report that the recovered code depends on inherited word-boundary structure; do not call it boundary-free glyph code.

positiveDoesSupport: a finite transferable operational transition system in the raw inscription sequence
glyph identities with measurable residual consequences beyond generic immediate context
a frozen quotient of glyph identities into action-equivalent classes if the class gate passes
positiveDoesNotByItselfSupply: historical intent of any individual inscription
a claim that every visual stroke is executable
claimLimits.historicalFunctionRule: A later contextual rejoin may compare frozen operator/classes to conventional readings. The empirical function is the transition law itself; any gloss remains separately sourced.

falsifiers.sourceDrift: Abort if the pinned upstream Git blob hash changes.
falsifiers.semanticLeakage: Abort if a forbidden source field appears in the blind packet or if induction reads the raw upstream file.
falsifiers.laneLeakage: Abort if holdout/control participates in vocabulary, eligibility, class-count selection, fingerprints, or class membership.
falsifiers.contextExplainsAll: If glyph-specific kernels do not beat P0 on holdout, the code claim fails under this state representation.
falsifiers.memorization: If gains are concentrated in fewer than the required fraction of independent inscriptions, do not call the operator transferable.
falsifiers.classCollapse: If finite classes fail to retain the required operator gain, do not claim a compact action-equivalence quotient.
